nodes.description: Peripheral motor and sensory neurons with long axons, and the Schwann cells that ensheathe them, are the initiating site of the neuropathy. COA7 is expressed in the cytoplasm of Schwann cells in human sural nerve, and neuron-specific knockdown of the fly orthologue impairs motor neuron terminals and locomotion, supporting a requirement in neurons. Oxidative stress, which the module records at this node, has not been examined in COA7 disease.

nodes.description: Pathogenic COA7 missense and in-frame alleles produce proteins that are imported into the mitochondrial intermembrane space more slowly than wild type through the MIA (CHCHD4) disulfide-relay pathway; mutant protein left in the cytosol is degraded by the proteasome, so little or no COA7 accumulates in mitochondria. In fibroblasts from the first reported patient no COA7 protein was detectable. Truncating alleles are presumed to abolish the protein, but this has not been tested.
